title: The padlock doesn't mean a website is safe
description: The HTTPS padlock proves your connection is encrypted, not that the site is honest. Here's what it really tells you.

scenes.say: That little padlock in your browser? It does not mean a website is safe.

left.label: Proves
items: Nobody can alter it en route

right.label: Doesn't
items: The owner is who they say

scenes.say: It proves your connection to that domain is encrypted, and can't be tampered with on the way. It says nothing about who runs the site, or what they'll do with your data.
Certificates are often issued automatically, after a check that you control the domain. So scammers get padlocks too. Plenty of phishing sites use HTTPS.
Chrome even replaced its padlock with a neutral settings icon, because most people misunderstood it. What matters is the address itself.
So type addresses yourself, check the domain carefully, and use bookmarks or official apps. Follow for more plain text threats.
